papers.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions

summary.tldr: Program-as-Weights (PAW) compiles natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts for fuzzy functions, matching larger LLM performance with significantly reduced inference memory and cost.
key_points: PAW uses a 4B compiler trained on FuzzyBench, a 10M-example dataset.
A 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter executes PAW programs.
PAW matches the performance of direct prompting Qwen3-32B.
PAW uses 1/50th of the inference memory compared to Qwen3-32B direct prompting.
PAW runs at 30 tokens/s on a MacBook M3.
summary.why_it_matters: This enables efficient, local execution of fuzzy functions previously outsourced to large language model APIs, reducing cost and improving reproducibility.

papers.title: AgenticSTS: A Bounded-Memory Testbed for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AgenticSTS introduces a bounded-memory testbed for long-horizon LLM agents, using typed retrieval for fresh user messages to isolate memory component effects in a complex game environment.
key_points: The testbed uses a bounded-memory contract where each decision is made from a fresh user message assembled by typed retrieval, avoiding raw cross-decision transcript appending.
The prompt remains bounded across runs of any length, allowing isolation and ablation of individual memory components.
The testbed is instantiated in Slay the Spire 2, a stochastic deck-building game requiring hundreds of decisions, where frontier LLMs currently show zero wins at the lowest difficulty.
A fixed-A0 ablation showed strategic skills increased wins from 3/10 to 6/10 games, indicating their impact on long-horizon decision-making.
A reproducible testbed is released, including 298 completed trajectories, memory/skill snapshots, prompt records, and analysis scripts.
summary.why_it_matters: This methodology provides a validated, reusable approach for studying how explicit memory layers influence long-horizon LLM-agent decisions in complex, sequential tasks.

papers.title: Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models

summary.tldr: FlashMorph optimizes hybrid attention model layer selection by formulating it as a budget-constrained subset optimization problem, improving long-context efficiency and performance over heuristic methods.
key_points: FlashMorph addresses hybrid layer selection as a budget-constrained subset optimization problem, moving beyond heuristic strategies like fixed patterns or isolated layer scoring.
It constructs a morphable model by adding a linear-attention branch to each full-attention layer, then freezes weights and optimizes layerwise gates on synthetic long-context retrieval data.
A linearization regularization encourages reliance on linear attention for efficiency during gate optimization.
Learned gates are discretized based on a full-attention budget to define the hybrid architecture, followed by logits distillation and long-context finetuning.
FlashMorph discovers more effective hybrid configurations, maintaining strong long-context recall and general benchmark performance while reducing layer selection cost.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more effective and efficient way to convert Transformer models into hybrid attention architectures, improving long-context processing without significant performance degradation.

papers.title: EvoPolicyGym: Evaluating Autonomous Policy Evolution in Interactive Environments

summary.tldr: EvoPolicyGym introduces Autonomous Policy Evolution, a controlled evaluation setting and benchmark for agents to iteratively improve executable policies in interactive RL environments under a fixed interaction budget.
key_points: EvoPolicyGym evaluates how agents iteratively improve explored policies within compact interactive RL environments.
The evaluation uses a harness-model agent that repeatedly edits an executable policy system under a fixed interaction budget.
GPT-5.5 achieved the strongest aggregate rank score and top-two performance across all 16 environments in the EvoPolicyGym suite.
EvoPolicyGym provides trajectory-level diagnostics to analyze budget allocation and feedback conversion into parametric tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework offers a standardized method to assess autonomous agents' ability to evolve policies, moving beyond simple final scores to understand the iterative improvement process.

papers.title: Multi-Resolution Flow Matching: Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration via Staged Sampling

summary.tldr: MrFlow is a training-free multi-resolution acceleration strategy for flow-matching models, achieving 10x speedup by generating low-resolution structures, super-resolving in pixel space, and refining details at high resolution.
key_points: MrFlow employs a staged low-to-high-resolution pipeline for pretrained flow-matching models.
The method first generates main structures at low resolution, then super-resolves in pixel space using a lightweight GAN-based model.
It injects low-strength noise for high-frequency resampling and refines details at high resolution.
MrFlow achieves 10x end-to-end acceleration on FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image, maintaining OneIG within a 1% gap.
It can be combined with pre-trained timestep distillation for up to 25x generation acceleration.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly accelerates text-to-image diffusion without training, reducing computational costs and improving efficiency for practical applications.

papers.title: AgenticDataBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Data Agents

summary.tldr: AgenticDataBench is a new comprehensive benchmark for LLM-based data agents, featuring realistic tasks from 15 diverse domains, including 5 B2B fintech use cases, with fine-grained ground-truth labels and skill-aligned evaluation.
key_points: AgenticDataBench collects real datasets and tasks from 15 vertical domains, including 5 real-world B2B use cases from a leading fintech company.
Data science skills are extracted from large-scale task solutions on Stack Overflow using skill-aligned hierarchical clustering to quantify benchmark coverage.
For real-world business tasks, task-solution pairs are selected to maximize diversity in skill composition.
A systematic LLM-based task generation approach creates workflows and tasks based on identified skills for domains lacking real tasks.
The benchmark enables evaluation of state-of-the-art data agents, providing detailed skill-level insights.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a standardized and comprehensive method to rigorously evaluate and compare LLM-based data agents across diverse and complex data science workflows.

papers.title: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory

summary.tldr: WorldDirector is a video world model framework that decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation, using an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories for controllable video synthesis with persistent dynamic object memory.
key_points: WorldDirector explicitly decouples semantic motion orchestration from visual generation, unlike existing world models that entangle physical dynamics with pixel rendering.
The framework leverages an LLM to coordinate 3D trajectories with camera movements.
Orchestrated trajectories serve as control signals for video generation, ensuring physical logic and appearance stability.
The method preserves exact visual identities of dynamic entities even after prolonged periods out of view.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables the synthesis of complex and extended events with enhanced controllability and persistent dynamic object memory, addressing limitations in existing world models.

papers.title: Breaking Failure Cascades: Step-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Medical Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: Medical Reasoning-aware Policy Optimization (MRPO) is an RL algorithm that uses step-wise process rewards to penalize early-stage reasoning failures, improving medical multimodal large language model performance and reducing error cascades.
key_points: MRPO assigns exponentially larger penalties to tokens in earlier invalid reasoning steps when the final answer is incorrect, specifically targeting cascading errors.
MRPO consistently outperforms standard GRPO and a recent RL baseline across three multimodal LLM backbones.
On Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, MRPO improves performance by 2.79 points over HuatuoGPT-Vision-34B.
MRPO reduces early-stage reasoning failures from 64.0% to 13.0%.
summary.why_it_matters: By mitigating early-stage reasoning failures, MRPO enhances both the reasoning quality and final answer accuracy of medical multimodal LLMs, crucial for clinical applications.

papers.title: SkillCoach: Self-Evolving Rubrics for Evaluating and Enhancing Agentic Skill-Use

summary.tldr: SkillCoach introduces a self-evolving rubric framework to evaluate and enhance LLM agent skill-use by analyzing skill selection, following, composition, and reflection, distinguishing process quality from task success.
key_points: SkillCoach derives skill-grounded process rubrics from real agent rollouts.
Evaluation of agent trajectories is performed across four dimensions: skill selection, skill following, skill composition, and skill-grounded reflection.
The framework separates external verifier success (outcome signal) from process quality.
Evolved rubrics provide process supervision for selecting high-quality training trajectories.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework improves evaluation quality, exposes hidden failures, and offers stronger supervision for enhancing agentic skill-use compared to outcome-only filtering.

papers.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill

summary.tldr: AutoMem automates learning memory management as a skill for LLMs, improving performance on long-horizon tasks by optimizing memory structure and agent proficiency.
key_points: AutoMem treats memory management as a trainable skill, promoting file-system operations as first-class memory actions.
The framework uses a two-loop automation process: one loop for a strong LLM to revise memory structure from trajectories, and another for training the agent's memory proficiency from good decisions.
Optimizing memory alone improved base agent performance by 2x-4x across Crafter, MiniHack, and NetHack games.
A 32B open-weight model with AutoMem achieved performance competitive with Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates that memory management is an independently learnable skill for LLMs, yielding significant performance gains in long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: PACE: A Proxy for Agentic Capability Evaluation

summary.tldr: PACE is a framework that constructs proxy benchmarks from non-agentic evaluation instances to predict LLM agentic performance, significantly reducing evaluation cost and time.
key_points: PACE selects a compact subset of non-agentic evaluation instances to predict scores on agentic benchmarks.
The framework uses a regression model to map scores from selected instances to target agentic benchmark scores.
Instance selection combines target-relevance local selection and globally informative global selection strategies.
Experiments across 14 models and 4 agentic benchmarks show PACE-Bench predicts agentic scores with <4% MAE, >0.80 Spearman correlation, and ~85% ranking accuracy.
PACE-Bench achieves these predictions at <1% of the cost of full agentic evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: PACE allows reliable estimation of agentic performance during model development and selection without the high cost and time of full agent evaluation.

papers.title: Logit-Contribution Scoring Identifies Non-Literal Retrieval Heads

summary.tldr: Logit-Contribution Scoring (LOCOS) is introduced as a write-aware detector for identifying attention heads responsible for non-literal retrieval in large language models, outperforming prior literal-copy based methods.
key_points: LOCOS scores heads by projecting their OV-circuit output onto the answer-token unembedding direction, contrasting needle and off-needle source positions.
LOCOS identifies heads that synthesize answers from context meaning rather than literal copy-pasting, addressing a limitation of existing detectors.

Ablating top LOCOS heads on the NoLiMa non-literal retrieval benchmark collapses ROUGE-L at lower head counts than prior attention-based detections (e.g., Qwen3-8B ROUGE-L from 0.401 to 0.000 with 50 ablated heads).
The identified heads are retrieval-specific, as ablating them does not significantly impact parametric recall or arithmetic reasoning.
Ablation of LOCOS heads on Qwen3-8B also drops MuSiQue from 0.55 to 0.08 and BABI-Long from 0.62 to 0.20, while random controls stay within 0.05 of baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more accurate way to interpret long-context model behavior by identifying the specific mechanisms responsible for non-literal information synthesis.

papers.title: Optimizing Visual Generative Models via Distribution-wise Rewards

summary.tldr: A novel framework finetunes generative models using distribution-wise rewards and a subset-replace strategy to improve image diversity and mitigate mode collapse, achieving FID-50K improvements.
key_points: The method employs distribution-wise rewards instead of sample-wise rewards to align generative models with real-world data distributions and mitigate mode collapse.
A subset-replace strategy is introduced to efficiently estimate distribution-wise rewards by updating only a small subset of a generated reference set.
RL is applied to optimize post-hoc model merging coefficients, addressing train-inference inconsistency from SDEs in standard RL.
Experiments show FID-50K improvements from 8.30 to 5.77 for SiT and from 3.74 to 3.52 for EDM2.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enhances the perceptual quality and diversity of images generated by visual generative models, leading to more realistic and varied outputs.

papers.title: AGVBench: A Reliability-Oriented Benchmark of Data Augmentation for Vein Recognition

summary.tldr: AGVBench evaluates 30 data augmentation strategies on five vein datasets and seven backbone architectures, revealing multi-image mixing methods offer strong recognition but poor calibration and adversarial vulnerability, highlighting the insufficiency of accuracy-centric evaluation.
key_points: AGVBench evaluates 30 augmentation strategies across five public palm/finger-vein datasets and seven backbone architectures (CNNs, vision transformers, vein-specific models).
Multi-image mixing methods (MixUp, PuzzleMix, StarMixup) generally achieve the strongest recognition performance.
Multi-image mixing methods are often poorly calibrated and vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, indicating a discrepancy between clean accuracy and adversarial security.
Severe geometric transformations frequently degrade vein recognition, potentially due to feature misalignment or spatial cropping.
Augmentation effectiveness varies between palm and finger vein datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: AGVBench provides standardized protocols to guide the design of reliable, secure, and robust vein recognition systems, moving beyond accuracy-centric evaluation.

papers.title: When Search Agents Should Ask: DiscoBench for Clarification-Aware Deep Search

summary.tldr: DiscoBench is a new benchmark for evaluating LLM-powered search agents on their ability to detect ambiguity, ask clarification questions, and recover correct reasoning paths in deep search scenarios.
key_points: DiscoBench contains 211 samples and 463 ambiguity instances across 11 real-world domains, covering four ambiguity types.
A user simulator is designed for multi-turn interaction to evaluate model performance.
Evaluation metrics include task utility, ambiguity detection, interaction strategy, and cost efficiency.
Experiments show ambiguity detection and effective clarification are distinct capabilities, and repeated searching without clarification performs worse than direct guessing.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark addresses a critical gap in current search agents, where their retrieval ability often fails in interactive problem-solving due to vague or underspecified user queries.

papers.title: Reading Between the Dots: Decoding Hidden Computation across Filler Tokens

summary.tldr: Frontier LLMs perform hidden computation over filler tokens, which is decodable from the residual stream with 80-95% accuracy, challenging behavioral CoT monitoring assumptions.
key_points: DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2 perform multi-step reasoning over content-free filler tokens (dots, counting sequences) for fact retrieval, numeric composition, string manipulation, and in-context computation.
Attention mechanisms route questions through filler regions to answers, and logit-lens readouts show fact retrieval and composition in late layers.
KV-cache transplants at filler positions causally swap outputs, demonstrating the computational role of these tokens.
An unsupervised decoding pipeline recovers intermediate values from hidden states with 80-95% accuracy across tasks and models, without ground-truth labels or training.
summary.why_it_matters: Monitorability of LLM computation extends beyond surface tokens to the full computational trace, enabling oversight of reasoning even when no explicit CoT is present.

papers.title: SPORK: Self-Speculative Forking to Accelerate Agentic LLM Inference

summary.tldr: SPORK introduces self-speculative forking for LLM agents, using the model itself to predict and pre-execute tool calls, reducing idle GPU time without auxiliary predictors or retraining.
key_points: SPORK uses a forked probe at generation start to predict upcoming tool names with 74.6-99.6% accuracy for Qwen3-32B across five benchmarks.
The system dispatches speculated tool calls early, overlapping execution with chain-of-thought decoding, and includes a prefix-cache fork, confidence gate, and partial-token accept mechanism.
SPORK reduces Qwen3-32B's GAIA P95 by 18% (131.9 to 108.1 s) on real-tool benchmarks, maintaining task accuracy within 1 pp of baseline.
The mechanism is effective across model sizes (4B-32B) and model types (dense, MoE), and is orthogonal to token-level speculative decoding.
summary.why_it_matters: SPORK significantly accelerates LLM agent inference by proactively executing tool calls, addressing a major bottleneck in Thought-Action-Observation loops without requiring model retraining or external predictors.

papers.title: How Much of the Routing Gap Is Real? Decomposing the Router-to-Oracle Gap into Reproducible Specialist Advantage and Single-Draw Label Noise

summary.tldr: 12-36% of the LLM router-to-oracle gap is single-draw label noise, not recoverable by single-commit routers but by test-time sampling, with a protocol released to measure it.
key_points: The expected oracle decomposes into reproducible single-commit headroom ($O^{\mathrm{repro}}$) and a non-negative single-commit selection floor ($\Delta$).
A recoverability asymmetry exists: the floor ($\Delta$) is not closed by any single-commit router but is recovered by test-time sampling (best-of-$K$).
Single-draw label noise accounts for 12-36% of the router-to-oracle gap on real open-model pools.
A multi-sample oracle protocol is released for routing benchmarks, re-estimating with fresh $k\ge20$ resampling under one-sided, dependence-corrected bounds.
Single-draw noise is a substantial minority of the gap, larger on unsaturated benchmarks and approaching half on the hardest queries across arithmetic, competition math, and non-math science.
LLMRouterBench's 20-point gap is a union of stochastic draws, requiring re-estimation since $O^{\mathrm{repro}}$ is non-identifiable at $k=1$.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a method to accurately measure the recoverable portion of the router-to-oracle gap, enabling more effective LLM routing strategies.

papers.title: Unbiased Alignment for Large Language Models with Noisy Preferences

summary.tldr: A theoretical framework introduces Unbiased Reward Model (URM) and Unbiased Direct Preference Optimization (UDPO) losses to correct for noise in human preference datasets, enabling unbiased LLM alignment.
key_points: Introduces Unbiased Reward Model (URM) loss and Unbiased Direct Preference Optimization (UDPO) loss.
Mathematically corrects distortion from preference noise in alignment methods.
Methods are noise-tolerant, parameter downward compatible, and classification-calibrated.
Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in experiments across diverse datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This allows for more robust and accurate large language model alignment using real-world, noisy human preference data.

papers.title: Variable Bit-width Quantization: Learning Per-Group Precision for "Bigger-but-Smaller" Language Models

summary.tldr: Variable Bit-width Quantization (VBQ) learns per-group precision for language models, enabling heterogeneous bit allocations that yield "bigger-but-smaller" models with improved efficiency.
key_points: VBQ is a training-time method where each 64-weight group learns its bit-width from {1,2,4,8} bits via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation and alternating optimization.
The method discovers highly heterogeneous precision allocations; for example, 69% of groups use 1 bit, the LM head averages 1.09 bits, and the first MLP block uses ~2.5 bits.
A 131M model at 1.82 mean bits achieves 4.2 PPL on TinyStories, outperforming a 55M FP16 model (4.4 PPL) with 3.8x less storage.
VBQ provides 3.9-8.4x more efficiency (quality-per-byte) than FP16 and accelerates inference with custom kernels, showing speedups up to 4.7x at 9B parameters on Apple silicon.
Deeper layers progressively self-heal quantization error from earlier layers, as revealed by distributional analysis (KL divergence, argmax-flip rate).
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows for significantly more efficient language models in terms of storage and inference speed while maintaining or improving performance compared to larger FP16 models.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Model Behaviors with Task-Specific Self-Reports

summary.tldr: The Stabilized Adapter for self-Report (SAR) is a lightweight LoRA adapter that enables fine-tuned language models to self-report hidden behaviors, detecting all seven implanted behaviors, including generalized misalignment.
key_points: SAR is a lightweight LoRA adapter designed to make fine-tuned models describe their own hidden behaviors in plain language.
SAR utilizes only the model and its training dataset for self-reporting.
SAR successfully detects all seven implanted hidden behaviors, even when the model exhibits broad misalignment not predicted by training data.
SAR improves upon Introspection Adapters (IA) by retaining positive signal where IA fails and roughly halving hallucination rates.
summary.why_it_matters: This provides a more reliable tool for auditing fine-tuned models to understand their learned behaviors and potential misalignments.

papers.title: RADIO1D: Elastic Representations for Condensed Vision Modeling

summary.tldr: RADIO1D compresses images into compact, variable-length 1D token sequences using multi-teacher knowledge distillation and an autoencoder, enabling flexible accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs in vision-language models.
key_points: Vision encoders in VLMs develop abstract, less spatially coherent representations, with specialized tokens summarizing global image content (e.g., SigLIP2).
RADIO1D uses multi-teacher knowledge distillation and an autoencoder to compress images into a variable-length 1D token sequence.
The 1D representations provide hierarchical summarization, allowing accurate scene understanding even with a single token.
RADIO1D offers adjustable token counts for flexible accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs in VLMs, improving performance and reducing computational overhead.
It supports improved composition-aware image retrieval.
summary.why_it_matters: This method allows for more efficient and accurate vision-language models by reducing computational overhead and providing flexible performance scaling.

papers.title: They Infer What You Meant: Models Represent Communicative Intent More Reliably Than They Act On It

summary.tldr: Language models robustly represent communicative intent in hidden states, but often fail to act on it in their default outputs; steering these internal representations can recover intended behavior.
key_points: A linear probe decodes communicative intent (e.g., recognize/evaluate) from hidden states across six models and four model families, even in base checkpoints, demonstrating robust representation.
Intent is decodable several layers before it drives model output, indicating a representational depth that precedes behavioral manifestation.
The failure to act on intent is model-specific, observed in three out of six tested models, and is not correlated with scaling laws.
Steering a discriminative direction, near-orthogonal to feedback-offering axes, at a specific layer recovers intended behavior as effectively as explicit instructions, even without a prompt.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and manipulating internal representations of communicative intent can lead to more aligned and responsive language model behavior without relying solely on prompt engineering.

papers.title: PORTS: Preference-Optimized Retrievers for Tool Selection with Large Language Models

summary.tldr: PORTS introduces an odds ratio preference optimization method for training tool selection retrievers, using a perplexity-inspired signal from a frozen LLM to improve alignment and accuracy.
key_points: PORTS fine-tunes a retriever using an odds ratio preference optimization method.
The preference signal is derived from a perplexity-inspired metric from a frozen LLM.
Optimization correlates selection probabilities with downstream performance and includes a contrastive semantic loss for documentation strings.
Evaluated across six datasets, two encoder models, and three LLMs, demonstrating improved tool selection accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a computationally efficient way to improve LLM tool selection, enabling better generalization to new queries and evolving toolsets in practical applications.

papers.title: MentalThink: Shaping Thoughts in Mental SVG World

summary.tldr: MentalThink introduces a visual-symbolic reasoning paradigm for MLLMs using a think-with-SVG pipeline to generate, render, and interpret scalable vector graphics as an intermediate visual representation for multi-turn reasoning.
key_points: MentalThink employs a think-with-SVG pipeline, enabling MLLMs to generate, render, and interpret SVG code for intermediate visual representation.
The system uses structured vector sketches to externalize spatial hypotheses, inspect them via deterministic rendering, and reason within a constrained geometric space.
Training involves a two-stage framework: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) for SVG syntactic alignment and multi-turn Reinforcement Learning (RL) for iterative inspection and refinement.
MentalThink achieved 55.1% on VSIBench and 76.0% on MindCube, demonstrating superior performance in spatial understanding and reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides MLLMs with a verifiable visual workspace for dynamic perspective taking, visual reflection, and compositional scene construction, mimicking human mental imagery.

summary.tldr: PyTorch's test infrastructure dynamically generates tests at import time, leading to device/dtype-specific names in CI that differ from source templates, which can be debugged locally using `pytest -k` or `test/run_test.py`.
key_points: PyTorch tests are often generated dynamically across devices and dtypes using `instantiate_device_type_tests()`, meaning CI test names may differ from source file names.
A single test method can expand across multiple devices, dtypes, and operators automatically via OpInfos and decorators, validating thousands of combinations.
For local debugging, filtering by the generated test name pattern using `pytest -k "test_name_pattern"` is more effective than targeting original template classes.

Device-generic tests allow writing one test method with device and dtype parameters, which `instantiate_device_type_tests()` expands into concrete device-specific classes and methods (e.g., `test_basic_cuda_float32`).
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding PyTorch's test generation and naming conventions is crucial for efficient debugging and contribution to the framework.
